log.msg: The transparent patches are `.checkered` on the wrong box. two.js built each pane as `demo-sim checkered`; the board answers "did this render paint its own background", but on the PANE it answered about the room the pane has that the simulated screen does not use. Measured at a 3000px window: the phone pane's box is 744px against a 390px screen — 354px of checkers. Under the render it is the `.demo-size` readout row, ~29px, on every layout page at every width.

It cannot move onto the render either: `zoom: 0.17` smears the 1.5em tile into an unreadable mesh — verified on the `wall` two-up at /framework/ext/demo/. And the question it asks is already answered for every twin: layout.js paints `--surface` on the frame precisely because a simulated screen has a ground. So the board leaves the two-up entirely.

No edge, measured: the layout paints --surface #ffffff and the page under it is --wash #f2f2f2 — 13/255 apart — and the stage is `bleed`, so there is no border either. Dark is better but still weak (#262626 on #171717). Non-twin layout exhibits (Stack, Sidebar) are worse: frame() paints nothing at all for them, so the render IS the page background.
Ground rendered two ways for Mike — `--line` (a soft step) and `--bg` (a device canvas). Verdict: --bg.

log.msg: Mike: --bg over --line. And the panes came off the ground's left and right edges as the handle moved — the 1:1 cap. It exists for the stage's width buttons (a phone in a wide PAGE should not be magnified), but in a two-up the panes ARE the stage, so the cap is dropped: room is the pane's own clientWidth, uncapped, and the readout still prints the factor (390px · 122%). The outward-alignment CSS it needed is deleted.

Verified: handle dragged to four positions at 1600 and 3000 — pane width == drawn width at every one, so no slack anywhere. 20/20 layout pages console-clean, fullscreen correct in both modes. The width readout took a literal white on the ground: --subtle was dark on dark, and --bg is a dark surface in BOTH modes, so this ink does not flip with the theme.

assign.outcome: **The two-up sits on a ground and always fills it.** Three faults, one shape: `.checkered` rode the PANE, so what it showed was the room a 1:1-capped fit left over (354px beside a phone at 3000) — dropped, since `layout.js` already paints a ground on every twin frame. A `bleed` exhibit's screen now takes `--bg`, so a specimen has an edge against a page it was 13/255 away from. And the fit is uncapped, so both panes fill their boxes at every handle position.
